newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung still seeks Fokker takeover.
newsitem.headline: Samsung still seeks Fokker takeover.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries continues to seek a takeover of bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker NV despite the pullout of a key supplier, a Samsung executive said on Friday.
"Takeover talks with Fokker administrators have not completely collapsed," the executive, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
"It's true that we have run into difficulties but our takeover plan still stands."

Fokker administrators have said they broke off negotiations with Samsung Aerospace after Belfast-based aerospace firm Short Brothers Plc had said it would no longer supply wings for Fokker aircraft. Short Brothers is part of Bombardier Inc of Canada.
Dutch administrators of Fokker said on Thursday Samsung had informed them that they would require another month to decide on whether to take over Fokker.
The Samsung executive did not explain how Samsung planned to take over and run a company that has no chance of staying in business after its wing supplier had left.
The Fokker administrators said in a statement they were forced to conclude that a re-launch of Fokker of the basis of continuing current production was no longer feasible.

Administrators who have been running Fokker since it was declared bankrupt in March gave Samsung the exclusive right to examine Fokker's books in September with a view to a possible bid for its core plane-making business.

But the talks have been deadlocked because Samsung failed to seek domestic partners in the takeover and drum up support from the government, industry sources said. Seoul government officials were not immediately available for comment.
Fokker is one of the oldest names in the industry and its F27 Friendship turboprop, launched in 1957, was one of the industry's biggest commercial successes.
